## NVENCForge 2.2.4: old WMV files, old Windows, old graphics cards

A round of fixes from a full read-through of the code and from a user's report. Thank you, Joan.

- **Old WMV files are no longer encoded at 1000 fps.** Some WMV files report their millisecond timebase as the frame rate and no average at all. The encode then really filled up to 1000 frames per second: in a rebuilt case 200 frames became 7991 and the file 13 times the size. NVENCForge now counts the frames when the reported rate cannot be true, and uses the counted rate for the measurement and the encode. Every other file is untouched.
- **A graphics card that only does 8-bit H.265 is used again.** The start-up check always tested 10 bit, even with `-8bit` or `bitDepth=8`. Cards like the GTX 950/960 failed it and were sent to the processor although they could have done the work.
- **FFmpeg does not start on an older Windows: the message now helps.** It says what the downloaded build requires (Windows 10 22H2 or newer) and where to get a different one to put next to `NVENCForge.exe`.
- **Answers to questions are no longer swallowed.** After a track question had timed out, the next answer you typed could vanish. Behind a front end such as NVENCForgeGUI this could leave the converter waiting forever on a PC without an Nvidia card.
- **No half-written FFmpeg after an interrupted download.** The files are only put in place once they are complete.
- **The settings file is replaced in one step.** Several converters starting at the same moment can no longer read a half-written `NVENCForge_Config.ini` and run one file on default values.

Update: replace `NVENCForge.exe` with the new one. Your settings stay. With NVENCForgeGUI: use the converter's update button.
